newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state sells majority in paper firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state sells majority in paper firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state has sold its majority stake of 2.25 million shares in Simo/Middle East Paper for 22 pounds ($6.48) a share, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said on Sunday.
It said in a statement that the sale, part of the state's privatisation programme, was worth a total of 49.5 million pounds.

The government-owned Holding Company for Chemical Industries and the state's National Investment Bank offered investors last week between 300,000 shares and 2.25 million shares, equivalent to 10 percent and 75 percent, at a minimum price of 20 pounds per share.
Before the offering, the holding company owned 68.15 percent of Simo while the National Investment Bank had a 31.85 percent stake in the paper firm.
The state has also sold 300,000 shares or 10 percent of its stake in Simo to the firm's Employee Shareholder Association.
